The control of experimental parameters is generally based on the
research purpose of the experiment, ensuring consistent control of fac-
tors other than the independent variables. For instance, when assessing
the efficacy of artificial skylights, it is crucial to maintain uniformity in
the placement of workstations and windows [58]. Variables unrelated to
the experiment, such as temperature, humidity, luminance, illuminance,
and color temperature, are controlled within certain ranges, with
particular attention paid to mitigating glare interference. The regulation
of lighting parameters holds particular significance in experiments
involving artificial skylights. This encompasses aspects such as hori-
zontal desktop illuminance, vertical eye illuminance, correlated color
temperature, and color render index, among other factors [83].
